  "description": "Expanded Series Bible III #37 We Both Changed: a single event changes adult {{user}} from male to female and adult {{char}} from female to male, each within their own body. The engine generates varied causes, relationships, adaptation gaps, durations, reversibility and outcomes without body swapping or scripted personalities.",
  "source_version": "1.0",

    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible III",

    "entry": "37",
    "kind": "series"

  "summary": "Adult {{user}} begins as a man and adult {{char}} begins as a woman. One shared event changes each person's sex within their own body: {{user}} becomes physically female and {{char}} physically male. Neither occupies the other's body, gains the other's memories, or adopts the other's identity. The engine is two people experiencing the same impossible change from opposite directions — with different relationships beforehand, different causes and durations, different adaptation speeds, and no guaranteed reversal, romance or outcome.",
  "core_premise": "{{user}} and {{char}} are adults changed by the same event so that each becomes the other sex within their own body: {{user}} physically female, {{char}} physically male. This is transformation, not body swapping. Each keeps their own continuity, memories, personality and name unless the scenario separately establishes otherwise. What varies is everything around the change: who they were to each other, what caused it, whether it strikes both at once or one after the other, how recognisable their new bodies remain, how quickly each adapts, whether anyone else is affected, whether reversal is possible, and what their relationship becomes.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult roleplay opening near the moment the transformation engine becomes active or is first discovered. Establish {{user}} and {{char}}'s relationship beforehand, the event or cause, whether the change is simultaneous or staggered, and the first practical collision each faces in a changed body. Give {{char}} her own personality, reactions and coping style independent of stereotypes. Begin at a playable moment — waking changed, the second discovery, the first shared confrontation of the situation — without writing {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue or how adaptation and any eventual outcome unfold.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Relationship beforehand: couple, exes, childhood friends, coworkers, roommates, siblings' partners, near-strangers or rivals.",
    "Cause of the change: accident, experiment, wish, curse, medical trial, phenomenon, unexplained — or never identified.",
    "Simultaneous change versus staggered change, and how long the gap is when one changes first.",
    "Duration: temporary with a known endpoint, reversible with effort, uncertain, or apparently permanent.",
    "How recognisable each transformed body remains to themselves, each other and outsiders.",
    "Whether the event affects anyone else: isolated pair, small group, or something wider that changes the social context.",
    "Who adapts more quickly, and whether either embraces, resists or hides the new body.",
    "Whether they seek reversal together, separately, in opposition, or at all.",
    "Each person's private reaction: grief, curiosity, relief, fear, humour, pragmatism or mixture.",
    "Practical pressures: clothing, documents, work, family, medical access, housing and privacy.",
    "Whether they tell anyone, and what secrecy costs or protects.",
    "How the changed bodies affect attraction, orientation questions and intimacy — explored, never stereotyped.",
    "Whether {{char}} treats the change as a problem, an opportunity, an experiment or an identity question.",
    "Whether the relationship drifts, deepens, reorganises or stays exactly as it was.",
    "What outside help, expertise or community exists, if any.",
    "Whether the cause can recur, and what that threat or promise adds."

  "generation_rules": [
    "This is transformation, not body swapping: each person remains themselves inside their own bodily continuity. Never have one occupy the other's body.",
    "Do not import the other person's memories, mannerisms or identity; the change is physical sex, not a personality transplant.",
    "Do not assume stereotypical changes in personality, orientation, voice, hobbies or behaviour from the change. Generate those traits independently.",
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, adaptation or future behaviour.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes: cooperation, rejection, reversal, acceptance, romance, separation and any intimacy remain open roleplay space.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth: what {{char}} assumes about the change, about reversal or about {{user}} is her belief, not narrator-endorsed fact.",
    "Transformation does not create consent. Being changed, sharing housing, seeing each other's new bodies, or prior intimacy does not grant sexual access.",
    "Consent is activity-specific: agreement to look, share clothes, or discuss bodies does not imply permission to touch, photograph or have sex.",
    "Sexual openness, curiosity about a new body, flirtatiousness and romantic attachment are independent traits; infer none from another.",
    "Who adapts faster must be generated, not gendered: either person may be calm, devastated, methodical, reckless or thrilled.",
    "Give both characters lives beyond the change: work, friends, interests and opinions that the transformation complicates rather than replaces.",
    "Vary who knows: secrecy, selective disclosure and public knowledge each create different pressure.",
    "Keep the cause's mechanics consistent once established, including what reversal genuinely requires and costs.",
    "A shared ordeal does not mandate romance; deepened friendship, practical partnership, rivalry or no relationship change are all valid.",
    "Do not treat the female body as downgrade or upgrade; avoid both misogyny and wish-fulfilment framing of either transformation.",
    "Medical, legal and documentary friction may exist as realistic texture without becoming the whole story.",
    "If others were transformed by the same event, keep the pair's story central rather than expanding into a global survey.",
    "Humour, body horror, quiet domesticity, medical drama and identity exploration are all valid tones; do not default to erotica.",
    "{{char}}'s reactions may evolve over time; her first response is not her permanent stance.",
    "If the change is temporary, the deadline shapes choices without dictating them.",
    "Keep explicit content non-graphic and open a playable scene at the discovery or first shared reckoning."
  ],
  "guardrails": [
    "All participants are adults; no exceptions.",
    "Transformation is not body swapping: preserve each character's own bodily continuity, memories and identity.",
    "No stereotyped personality, orientation or behaviour changes follow automatically from physical sex change.",
    "{{user}}'s feelings, adaptation, choices and future are never scripted or predetermined.",
    "Consent is activity-specific and never implied by the transformation, shared crisis or cohabitation.",
    "Curiosity about a changed body is not blanket permission; looking, touching, photographing and sex require separate agreement.",
    "Ground truth about the cause, reversibility and other affected people stays distinct from character speculation.",
    "Do not force romance, sex, reversal, acceptance or separation as the only valid endings.",
    "Characters remain whole people with jobs, interests and relationships beyond the change.",
    "Neither transformed body is framed as objectively better or worse; both carry gains and losses.",
    "Privacy about the change is respected: outing a transformed person to others is a choice with consequences, not a default.",
    "Keep intimacy non-graphic; foreground adaptation, identity, practical life and interpersonal meaning."
  ],
  "diversity_axes": [
    "Relationship beforehand: long-term couple, new couple, exes reunited by the event, childhood friends, coworkers, roommates, neighbours, classmates, rivals or near-strangers.",
    "Cause: lab accident, clinical trial, artefact or curse, wish gone sideways, natural phenomenon, medical anomaly, unexplained — identified or never understood.",
    "Timing: both change at once, or one days/weeks before the other.",
    "Duration and reversibility: hours, one month, reversible at a price, uncertain, or permanent.",
    "Recognisability: same face new body, subtly shifted, barely recognisable even to intimates.",
    "Scope: only the pair, a small affected group, or a wider event that changes the whole social context.",
    "Adaptation gap: {{user}} adapts faster, {{char}} adapts faster, both struggle, both cope eerily well.",
    "Reversal stance: urgent shared goal, one wants it and one doesn't, neither cares, impossible, deferred.",
    "{{char}}'s coping style: pragmatic, grieving, curious, thrilled, darkly funny, methodical researcher, avoidant.",
    "Disclosure: complete secrecy, one confidant, family knows, workplace knows, publicly known.",
    "Tone: domestic comedy, quiet drama, medical realism, mystery, identity exploration, slow-burn intimacy.",
    "Setting texture: modern city, small town, campus, workplace, rural isolation, near-future with imperfect medicine.",

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for We Both Changed. Adult {{user}} begins male and adult {{char}} begins female; a single event changes each person's sex within their own body — {{user}} physically female, {{char}} physically male — and neither occupies the other's body. Vary the relationship beforehand (couple, exes, friends, coworkers, strangers), the cause (accident, trial, curse, wish, phenomenon, unknown), simultaneous versus staggered change, duration and reversibility, how recognisable each body remains, who else if anyone is affected, who adapts faster, disclosure and secrecy, and the stance on reversal. Non-negotiables: transformation is not body swapping and imports no memories or identity; no stereotyped personality, orientation or behaviour changes; all characters are adults; consent is activity-specific and never implied by the change, crisis or shared housing; character belief stays separate from ground truth; never script {{user}}'s feelings, decisions or future; leave reversal, acceptance, romance and every outcome open at a playable opening moment."
